case_name: State of Madhya Pradesh v Gwalior Sugar Company, Limited, and Others
facts: These are cross appeals from two judgments of the erstwhile High Court of Madhya Bharat.
In order to appreciate these contentions it is necessary to set out certain facts.
A sugar factory was established at Dabra in 1940.
The Maharaja Scindia constituted a Committee to consider the desirability of imposing a 'cane cess' on sugarcane purchased by the respondent factory.
The Report of the Committee was submitted to the Maharaja by the Chairman on July 23, 1946.
The Economic Adviser to the Government of Gwalior wrote a letter to the Manager of the respondent factory on August 26, 1946.
The respondent factory protested against this levy and made a representation to the Government of Madhya Bharat against the levy of the cess.
After the formation of the State of Madhya Pradesh, the respondent made a representation to the Government of Madhya Pradesh against the levy of the cess.
issues: Whether the order dated July 27, 1946, of the Gwalior Durbar was only an executive order and not a law under Art. 265 of the Constitution.
Whether the imposition of the cess violates the guarantee of equal protection contained in Art. 14 of the Constitution.
petitioner_arguments: The respondent factory argued that the cess was not levied under any law and is discriminatory against them.
The respondent factory argued that the State of Madhya Pradesh is not entitled to recover the cess due from the respondents after January 26, 1950.
respondent_arguments: The State of Madhya Pradesh argued that the order dated July 27, 1946, of the Gwalior Durbar was a law under Art. 265 of the Constitution.
The State of Madhya Pradesh argued that the imposition of the cess does not violate the guarantee of equal protection contained in Art. 14 of the Constitution.
court_reasoning: The Court held that the order dated July 27, 1946, of the Gwalior Durbar was a law under Art. 265 of the Constitution.
The Court held that the imposition of the cess does not violate the guarantee of equal protection contained in Art. 14 of the Constitution.
holding: The Court held that the cess was imposed by authority of law and is a perfectly valid one.
It would be competent to the State of Madhya Pradesh to realise that cess from the respondent factory.
cases_cited: It has recently been held by this Court in M. K. Prithi Rajji v. The
State of Madhya Pradesh v Gwalior Sugar Company
is covered by the decision of this Court in Madhaorao Phalke v. The
